objectives.text: Using the rules associated with basic DC circuit characteristics, ANALYZE various DC circuits to find resistances, currents, and voltages at any given point within the circuit.

enabling.text: LIST the four ways to produce a DC voltage.
STATE the purpose of a rectifier.
DESCRIBE the outputs of the following circuits:
Given a diagram, IDENTIFY it as one of the following types:
Given a circuit, DETERMINE whether the circuit is an open circuit or a closed circuit.
Given a circuit, CALCULATE total resistance for a series or parallel circuit.
DESCRIBE what is meant by the term "voltage divider."
DESCRIBE what is meant by the term "current division."
DESCRIBE the difference between electron flow and conventional current flow.
Given a circuit showing current flows, IDENTIFY the polarity of the voltage drops in the circuit.
Given a circuit, SOLVE problems for voltage and current using Kirchhoff’s laws.

DESCRIBE the voltage and current effects of an open in a DC circuit.

passages.quote: The purpose of a rectifier circuit is to convert AC power to DC.
The diode acts as a gate, which allows current to pass in one direction and blocks current in the other direction.
The output of a half-wave rectifier circuit is pulsating DC.
A full-wave rectifier circuit is a circuit that rectifies the entire cycle of the AC sine-wave.
This circuit utilizes four diodes.
There are four common ways that DC voltages are produced.
Schematic diagrams are the standard means by which we communicate information in electrical and electronics circuits.
There are four types of circuit diagrams.
The one-line, or single-line, diagram shows the components of a circuit by means of single lines and the appropriate graphic symbols.
A block diagram is used to show the relationship between component groups, or stages in a circuit.
A wiring diagram is a very simple way to show wiring connections in an easy-to-follow manner.
Resistivity is defined as the measure of the resistance a material imposes on current flow.
Temperature coefficient of resistance, α (alpha), is defined as the amount of change of the resistance of a material for a given change in temperature.
A closed circuit (Figure 13) is an uninterrupted, or unbroken, path for current from the source (EMF), through the load, and back to the source.
An open circuit, or incomplete circuit, (Figure 14) exists if a break in the circuit occurs; this prevents a complete path for current flow.
A series circuit is a circuit where there is only one path for current flow.
Parallel circuits are those circuits which have two or more components connected across the same voltage source
In all cases, the equivalent resistance will be less than any of the individual parallel circuit resistors.
The total resistance in a series circuit is equal to the sum of all the parts of that circuit
The sum of the voltage drops in any series circuit is always equal to the applied voltage.
Total resistance of equal resistors in a parallel circuit is equal to the resistance of one resistor divided by the number of resistors.
A voltage divider, or network, is used when it is necessary to obtain different values of voltage from a single energy source.
This process is known as current division.
each branch current is inversely proportional to the branch resistance.
The direction of positive charges, or holes, is in the opposite direction of electron flow.
where the electron current enters the load, the voltage is negative
The sum of the voltage drops around a closed loop is equal to the sum of the voltage sources of that loop
The current arriving at any junction point in a circuit is equal to the current leaving that junction
If the assumed direction is correct, the answer will be positive.
Solving these circuits can be simplified by reducing the circuit to a single equivalent resistance circuit
Since no current flows in an open series circuit, there are no voltage drops across the loads.
If a parallel circuit is opened at a point where only a branch current flows, then only that branch is open, and current continues to flow in the rest of the circuit
In a DC circuit, the only current limit is the circuit resistance.
the terminal voltage of the energy source will decrease.
Fuses are provided in circuits to protect against short circuits.
Parallel circuits are more likely than series circuits to develop damaging short circuits.

body.text: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
A DC generator delivers pulsating DC through commutator action. A thermocouple converts heat energy into a voltage output.
A diode is forward biased when the positive terminal of a voltage source is connected to its anode and the negative terminal to its cathode.
With reverse bias, the anode is connected to the negative side of the source, which causes a high resistance that prevents current flow.
With a single diode, current flows only during one-half of the input voltage cycle.

body.alt: A single diode rectifier with an AC input waveform. Current passes on the forward-biased half cycle only, giving pulses on one side of the axis.

body.text: The full-wave bridge rectifier is another type of full-wave rectifier circuit.

body.alt: Bridge rectifier of four diodes shown for each half cycle of the AC input, with current through the load in the same direction both times.

body.text: Its output is a pulsating DC, with all of the waves of the input AC being transferred.

checks.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four common ways to produce a DC voltage?
checks.x: The four common ways are batteries, DC generators, thermocouples, and rectifiers.

checks.q: How many diodes does a full-wave bridge rectifier use?
checks.x: The full-wave bridge rectifier circuit utilizes four diodes.

body.alt: Schematic diagram of a two-transistor radio circuit, using graphic symbols connected by lines, from antenna to headset.
One-line diagram of an electrical substation, with lightning arresters, disconnect switches, a transformer, and a circuit breaker on a single line.
Block diagram of rectangles for the stages of a radio receiver, joined by arrows from input to output.
Wiring diagram of an appliance circuit showing components in pictorial form, identified by name, with connecting wires.

body.text: Wiring diagrams show the component parts in pictorial form, and most also show the relative location of parts and the color coding of conductors.

checks.q: A diagram uses rectangles joined by lines with arrowheads to show circuit stages from input to output. What type is it?
checks.x: A block diagram shows the relationship between component groups, or stages in a circuit, from input to output.

checks.q: A diagram shows parts in pictorial form, identified by name. What type is it?
checks.x: Wiring diagrams show the component parts in pictorial form, and the components are identified by name.

body.text: The resistance of a conductor depends on its resistivity, its length, and its cross-sectional area.
A positive value means resistance increases with temperature, a negative value means it decreases, and zero means it is constant.
Each electrical circuit has at least four basic parts: a source of electromotive force, conductors, a load or loads, and some means of control.

body.alt: A closed loop of a battery, a switch, and a resistor load joined by conductors.
Three open circuits: one with an open switch, one with a burned-out fuse, and one with a burned-out resistor.

body.text: A short circuit offers very little resistance to current flow and can cause dangerously high current through a circuit.

body.alt: A battery and resistor R with a shorting connection across the resistor, and a fuse in the circuit.
Series circuit of a voltage source and resistors R1, R2, and R3 in one loop, with the same current I throughout.
Parallel circuit with resistors R1, R2, and R3 each across the same voltage source, with branch currents and a voltmeter on each branch.

body.text: Current through each branch can be different, but voltage throughout a parallel circuit is equal.

checks.q: A material has a positive temperature coefficient of resistance. What happens to its resistance as temperature rises?
checks.x: A positive value of the temperature coefficient of resistance indicates that resistance increases with temperature.

checks.q: A fuse in a circuit burns out. What kind of circuit results?
checks.x: A break in the circuit prevents a complete path for current flow, which makes it an open circuit.

body.text: The total voltage across a series circuit is equal to the sum of the voltages across each resistor.
The sum of the currents through each branch of a parallel circuit is equal to the total current flow in the circuit.
For two unequal resistors in parallel, multiply the two resistances and divide the product by the sum.
Sometimes branch currents in a parallel circuit must be found when only resistance and total current are known. The resistances divide the total current into fractional currents in each branch.
I1 = IT x R2 / (R1 + R2)
For a series-parallel circuit, follow the series rules for the series part and the parallel rules for the parallel part.

checks.q: What is the total resistance of 20, 30, and 50 ohm resistors in series?
What is the total resistance of a 6 ohm and a 3 ohm resistor in parallel?
When is a voltage divider used?
o: To obtain different values of voltage from a single energy source
To convert AC power to DC
checks.x: A voltage divider is used when it is necessary to obtain different values of voltage from a single energy source.

checks.q: A total current of 12 amps divides between a 2 ohm and a 4 ohm branch. What is the current in the 2 ohm branch?
checks.x: I1 = IT x R2 / (R1 + R2) = 12 x 4 / 6 = 8 amps. Each branch current is inversely proportional to the branch resistance.

checks.q: A 4 ohm resistor is in series with two 10 ohm resistors in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
checks.x: The parallel pair is 10/2 = 5 ohms. In series with 4 ohms, the total is 9 ohms.

body.text: The direction of electron flow is from a point of negative potential to a point of positive potential.
This flow of positive charges is known as conventional flow. Both conventions are in use and they are essentially equivalent.
To find the polarity of a voltage drop, use the direction of the electron current as a basis.

body.alt: Series circuit with a battery and resistors, marked with plus and minus at each resistor. The minus is where electron current enters.

body.text: The drop across the load is opposite to that of the source.

checks.q: How does conventional flow compare with electron flow?
o: It is in the same direction
It is in the opposite direction
It only occurs in AC circuits
checks.x: The direction of positive charges, or holes, is in the opposite direction of electron flow. This is conventional flow.

checks.q: Where electron current enters a load, what is the polarity of the voltage?
checks.x: Where the electron current enters the load, the voltage is negative.

body.text: Many circuits are extremely complex and cannot be solved with Ohm's Law. Kirchhoff's two laws solve them.
Law 1, Kirchhoff's voltage law:
ΣEsource = ΣIR
The voltage law can be applied only to closed loops. A closed loop must have one or more voltage sources and a complete path for current flow.
Law 2, Kirchhoff's current law:

body.alt: Arrows for current arriving at and leaving junctions. The total arriving equals the total leaving.

body.text: With more than one voltage source, a direction of current flow must be assumed. Sources that aid the assumed direction are positive, and sources that oppose it are negative.
A negative answer means the assumed direction was wrong, but the magnitude is correct.
Kirchhoff's laws are only restating the laws governing energy and charge conservation.

checks.q: Kirchhoff's voltage law says the sum of the voltage drops around a closed loop equals:
o: The sum of the voltage sources of that loop
The total resistance of the loop
checks.x: The sum of the voltage drops around a closed loop is equal to the sum of the voltage sources of that loop.

checks.q: 15 amps arrives at a junction with two paths leaving it. One path carries 10 amps. What does the other carry?
checks.x: The current arriving at a junction equals the current leaving it, so the other path carries 15 - 10 = 5 amps.

checks.q: A 30 volt source drives a loop with 5 ohm and 10 ohm resistors. Using Kirchhoff's voltage law, what is the current?
checks.x: ΣE = ΣIR gives 30 = 5I + 10I = 15I, so I = 2 amps.

body.text: A series circuit has only one path for current. If this path is broken, no current flows and the circuit becomes an open circuit.

body.alt: Three series circuits opened by an open switch, a burned-out fuse, and a burned-out resistor.

body.text: No power is consumed by the loads, and total power consumed by the circuit is zero.
If the resistance suddenly becomes zero, a very large current will flow.

body.alt: A battery and resistor R with a shorting connection across the resistor, and a fuse in the circuit.

body.text: With an increase in circuit current, the terminal voltage of the energy source will decrease, due to the voltage drop across its internal resistance.
The increased current from a short circuit can damage power sources, burn insulation, and start fires.
Each parallel load is connected directly across the power source. In a series circuit, the other loads keep the circuit resistance from dropping to zero.

checks.q: A parallel circuit opens at a point where only a branch current flows. What happens?
o: Only that branch is open, and current continues in the rest
The circuit becomes a short circuit
checks.x: Only that branch is open, and current continues to flow in the rest of the circuit.

checks.q: What happens to the terminal voltage of the source when a short circuit raises circuit current?
checks.x: With an increase in circuit current, the terminal voltage of the energy source will decrease, because of the voltage drop across its internal resistance.

checks.q: Which type of circuit is more likely to develop a damaging short circuit?
checks.x: Parallel circuits are more likely than series circuits to develop damaging short circuits, because each load is connected directly across the power source.

facts.a: Schematic, one-line, block, and wiring diagrams.

The measure of the resistance a material imposes on current flow.

summary.text: DC voltages are commonly produced by batteries, DC generators, thermocouples, and rectifiers.
A rectifier converts AC to DC. Half-wave rectifiers convert only one-half of the sine wave, and full-wave rectifiers convert all of it.
A closed circuit has a complete path for current flow, and an open circuit does not.
A series circuit has one path for current flow. A parallel circuit has two or more components across the same voltage source.
Where the electron current enters the load, the voltage is negative.
Kirchhoff's voltage law and current law restate the laws governing energy and charge conservation.
An open series DC circuit consumes no power, and a shorted DC circuit has a sudden and very large increase in current.

Page 61 says the delta network shapes resemble the Greek letters π and Ω, but the figure and heading say π and Δ. This content is not on the page.
Page 1 says a battery has cells connected in series, while ES-04 says connected voltaic cells and also covers parallel cells. The lesson does not repeat the series-only wording.
